bundle.author: swain
bundle.title: pr-reviewer evals: replay recorded reviews, judge variants pairwise
bundle.body:
## Why

Stacked on #243. That PR makes every review a replayable record: the agent's complete input is persisted, so a prompt or model change can be run against the same PRs the bot already reviewed and compared blind to what shipped. This adds the harness that does that.

A case is a production record. A variant is the ops ref you run the CLI from. `replay` re-runs the agent exactly as production does (same prompt builder, same read-only tools, same credential-stripped env) against the recorded bundle; `judge` compares two replays pairwise with the order-swapped, blinded judge already in `bugboss-evals`, under a rubric that penalises approving over a real bug most, false findings next, and never rewards finding count. The report is win rate plus an exact sign test, so twelve cases with ten wins one way is a result and six-six is not.

No corpus is seeded here; live records become the corpus after #243 cuts over.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> New offline/dev tooling and tests only; replay invokes the same agent stack as production when run manually but does not change the production review path.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **PR-reviewer eval harness** under `delegate/review/eval` so recorded production `ReviewRecord`s can be frozen, replayed on different git variants, and compared pairwise.
> 
> **`npm run review:eval`** exposes three flows: **`cases snapshot`** (pull/filter `ReviewRecord`s from S3 or a local dir into a corpus), **`replay`** (checkout each PR at `headSha`, run `pr-reviewer` like production via `buildReviewPrompt` / `agentEnv` / git MCP, write per-case `Result` JSON with resume/`--force` and concurrency), and **`judge`** (blind order-swapped passes using `bugboss-evals`’ judge + a new `rubric.md`, then a markdown report with win counts and a two-sided binomial sign test).
> 
> Tests cover case I/O, replay error/skip behavior, judge majority/unstable logic, and reporting. `package.json` wires the CLI script and includes `delegate/review/eval/*.test.ts` in `npm test`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 08e38d9559f36df516d5211c1fb85497fa0816b4. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

priorFindings.body: The fallthrough on line 124 is reached when `aWins != bWins` but neither a, b, nor tie has a strict plurality over both others — i.e. when one of a/b is tied with tieCount. For example, with the default 4 passes a result of 2a/0b/2tie reaches line 124 and returns `"a"`, even though ties matched a in frequency. This misrepresents an ambiguous plurality as a clear win; the correct result is `"unstable"`. Lines 120–123 each require strict majority over *both* other counts, so any two-way tie for the lead falls through to line 124 which silently picks whichever of a/b is larger. (Falsification: traced all guards — line 120 fails because `aWins > tieCount` is false; lines 121–122 fail similarly; line 123 requires `aWins === bWins` which is false when bWins=0; the only path left is the fallthrough.)

error: agent returned no JSON: The prior finding's bug is confirmed fixed — `deriveOverallWinner` now returns `"unstable"` on line 123 for any case where no category has strict plurality (e.g., 2a/0b/2tie).
